intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type Ib (CDAN1B) is caused by homozygous mutation in the CDIN1 gene (C15ORF41; 615626).

checks.claim: Congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type Ib (CDAN1B) is caused by homozygous mutation in the CDIN1 gene (C15ORF41).
checks.evidence_quote: We used whole genome sequencing and segregation analysis to identify a homozygous T to A transversion (c.533T>A), predicted to lead to a p.L178Q missense substitution in C15ORF41
checks.explanation: Homozygous C15ORF41 mutations were identified in CDAN1-negative CDA I pedigrees (p.L178Q, and p.Y94C in two further pedigrees). The 'type Ib' label and the CDIN1 symbol are standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Congenital dyserythropoietic anemia (CDA) type Ib is a form of CDA type I. Babbs et al. (2013) noted that CDA type Ia is caused by mutation in the CDAN1 gene. They found that CDA type Ib is caused by mutation in CDIN1 (C15ORF41), a gene that encodes a predicted endonuclease.

checks.claim: Congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type Ib is a form of CDA type I.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygous mutations in a predicted endonuclease are a novel cause of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I.
checks.explanation: The C15ORF41-related disease is presented as CDA type I, but the abstract never uses the subtype designation 'Ib'.

checks.claim: CDA type Ia is caused by mutation in the CDAN1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the CDAN1 gene, which encodes Codanin-1, underlie the majority of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I cases.
checks.explanation: CDAN1 mutations cause most CDA I; the 'Ia' label is nomenclature.

checks.claim: CDA type Ib is caused by mutation in CDIN1 (C15ORF41).
checks.evidence_quote: identify a homozygous T to A transversion (c.533T>A), predicted to lead to a p.L178Q missense substitution in C15ORF41
checks.explanation: C15ORF41 mutations were found in CDAN1-negative CDA I families.

checks.evidence_quote: Detailed sequence similarity searches indicate that C15ORF41 encodes a novel restriction endonuclease

paragraphs.text: Babbs et al. (2013) found homozygous mutations in individuals with CDA type I, including those in 1 consanguineous pedigree. This was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: Babbs et al. (2013) found homozygous CDIN1 (C15ORF41) mutations in individuals with CDA type I, including individuals in 1 consanguineous pedigree.
checks.evidence_quote: identify a homozygous T to A transversion (c.533T>A), predicted to lead to a p.L178Q missense substitution in C15ORF41, a gene of unknown function, in a consanguineous pedigree of Middle-Eastern origin.
checks.explanation: Stated directly; further homozygous mutations were found in two more families.

checks.claim: The homozygous CDIN1 (C15ORF41) mutations in CDA type I individuals were consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: identify a homozygous T to A transversion (c.533T>A), predicted to lead to a p.L178Q missense substitution in C15ORF41, a gene of unknown function, in a consanguineous pedigree of Middle-Eastern origin.
checks.explanation: Homozygosity in a consanguineous family is consistent with recessive inheritance, but the abstract does not state the inheritance pattern.

paragraphs.text: Ahmed et al. (2006) found evidence of genetic heterogeneity in congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I. Babbs et al. (2013) noted that mutations in the CDAN1 gene, which encodes codanin-1, cause most cases of CDA I (CDA type Ia). However, no likely pathogenic CDAN1 mutation was found in some patients with CDA I. Babbs et al. (2013) found that, in some of these CDAN1 mutation-negative patients, CDA I was caused by mutation in C15ORF41 (CDA Ib).

checks.claim: Ahmed et al. (2006) found evidence of genetic heterogeneity in congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I.
checks.evidence_quote: Evidence of genetic heterogeneity in congenital dyserythropoietic anaemia type I.
checks.explanation: The title states the finding directly. Only the title was supplied, so no details beyond that were checked.

checks.claim: Mutations in the CDAN1 gene cause most cases of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I (CDA type Ia).
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the CDAN1 gene, which encodes Codanin-1, underlie the majority of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I cases.
checks.explanation: Stated directly. The 'Ia' label is nomenclature.

checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the CDAN1 gene, which encodes Codanin-1

checks.claim: No likely pathogenic CDAN1 mutation was found in some patients with congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I.
checks.evidence_quote: However, no likely pathogenic CDAN1 mutation has been detected in approximately 20% of cases, suggesting the presence of at least one other locus.

checks.claim: In some CDAN1 mutation-negative patients with congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I, the disease was caused by mutation in C15ORF41 (CDA Ib).
checks.evidence_quote: Sequencing C15ORF41 in other CDAN1 mutation-negative congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I pedigrees identified a homozygous transition (c.281A>G), predicted to lead to a p.Y94C substitution, in two further pedigrees
checks.explanation: C15ORF41 mutations were found in CDAN1 mutation-negative CDA I pedigrees.

paragraphs.text: Babbs et al. (2013) studied patients with CDA I who did not have CDAN1 mutations. Using whole genome sequencing and segregation analysis, they identified homozygous missense mutations in the C15ORF41 gene in affected individuals, including a consanguineous pedigree of Middle-Eastern origin. Sequence similarity searches indicated that C15ORF41 encodes a novel restriction endonuclease belonging to the Holliday junction resolvase family of proteins. Babbs et al. (2013) concluded that homozygous mutations in this predicted endonuclease are a novel cause of CDA I.

checks.claim: Babbs et al. (2013) studied patients with CDA I who did not have CDAN1 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequencing C15ORF41 in other CDAN1 mutation-negative congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I pedigrees
checks.explanation: The study focused on CDAN1 mutation-negative CDA I.

checks.claim: Babbs et al. (2013) used whole genome sequencing and segregation analysis to study CDAN1 mutation-negative CDA I patients.
checks.evidence_quote: We used whole genome sequencing and segregation analysis to identify a homozygous T to A transversion (c.533T>A), predicted to lead to a p.L178Q missense substitution in C15ORF41, a gene of unknown function, in a consanguineous pedigree of Middle-Eastern origin.
checks.explanation: WGS and segregation analysis were used in the Middle-Eastern family; the other families were studied by sequencing C15ORF41 only.

checks.claim: Homozygous missense mutations in the C15ORF41 gene were identified in individuals affected with CDAN1 mutation-negative CDA I.
checks.evidence_quote: identified a homozygous transition (c.281A>G), predicted to lead to a p.Y94C substitution, in two further pedigrees of SouthEast Asian origin.
checks.explanation: Homozygous missense mutations (L178Q, Y94C) were found in CDAN1-negative CDA I.

checks.claim: A consanguineous pedigree of Middle-Eastern origin with CDA I carried a homozygous missense mutation in C15ORF41.
checks.evidence_quote: predicted to lead to a p.L178Q missense substitution in C15ORF41, a gene of unknown function, in a consanguineous pedigree of Middle-Eastern origin.

checks.claim: Sequence similarity searches indicated that C15ORF41 encodes a novel restriction endonuclease.
checks.evidence_quote: Detailed sequence similarity searches indicate that C15ORF41 encodes a novel restriction endonuclease

checks.claim: The predicted C15ORF41 protein belongs to the Holliday junction resolvase family of proteins.
checks.evidence_quote: a novel restriction endonuclease that is a member of the Holliday junction resolvase family of proteins.

checks.claim: Babbs et al. (2013) concluded that homozygous mutations in the predicted endonuclease C15ORF41 are a novel cause of CDA I.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygous mutations in a predicted endonuclease are a novel cause of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I.
checks.explanation: The paper's title states this conclusion.
